subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the equation of the line perpendicular to the line 3x+4y+6=0 and making an intercept −4 on the x-axis.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Very Short Answer question 42, book p.148. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The split gives one mark for the perpendicular family bx − ay + k = 0 and one for fixing k from the x-intercept. Perpendicularity was confirmed numerically, not assumed: m₁m₂ = (−3/4)(4/3) = −1, and the normals (3, 4) and (4, −3) have dot product 12 − 12 = 0. The answer was then checked by setting y = 0, which returns x = −4. This book prints almost no exam-appearance years, so appearances[] is empty. Paper position: Maths-1B Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say how you write a line perpendicular to a given one, and what an x-intercept of −4 means as a point.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the perpendicular family
steps.margin_note: First mark. Swap the coefficients and change exactly ONE sign. Then confirm m₁m₂ = −1 before going on — a swap with no sign change still passes through the point and looks right.
steps.memory_tip: Perpendicular: swap the coefficients and change exactly ONE sign. Then check m₁m₂ = −1.
lines: Any line perpendicular to ax + by + c = 0
has the form  bx − ay + k = 0

recall.must_convey: That the perpendicular line has the form 4x − 3y + k = 0, and that its slope times the given slope is −1.
accept: swap the coefficients and change one sign
the perpendicular line is four x minus three y plus k
the product of the slopes must be minus one
perpendicular ki coefficients swap chesi oka sign marchali
b x minus a y plus k equals zero

steps.why: Swapping the coefficients without changing a sign gives 4x + 3y + k = 0, which is a real line and can still be made to have the right intercept, so the error survives every later check. Computing m₁m₂ and seeing −1 is what rules it out.
common_mistakes: Writing 4x + 3y + k = 0, which swaps the coefficients but changes no sign.
Keeping 3x + 4y + k = 0, which is parallel to the given line, not perpendicular.

steps.label: Use the x-intercept
steps.margin_note: Second mark. An x-intercept of −4 is the point (−4, 0) on the line, so substitute the point and read off k.
steps.memory_tip: An x-intercept of −4 is the POINT (−4, 0). Substitute the point, not the number.

recall.must_convey: That (−4, 0) is substituted to give k = 16, so the line is 4x − 3y + 16 = 0.
accept: the x intercept minus four means the point minus four comma zero
substitute to get k equals sixteen
the line is four x minus three y plus sixteen equals zero
minus four comma zero substitute cheyyali
heard_as: four x minus three y plus sixteen

steps.why: The perpendicular family leaves exactly one unknown, and one point on the line is exactly enough to fix it; the x-intercept is that point written as a number.
common_mistakes: Substituting (0, −4), which is the y-intercept point.
Stopping at k = 16 without writing the equation of the line.
